chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Manṣūr, from Faḍl al-Aʿwar, from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said:

We were, at the time of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), when he passed away, wavering like sheep that have no shepherd. Then we met Sālim ibn Abī Ḥafṣah, and he said to me, “O Abū ʿUbaydah, who is your Imam?” So I said, “My Imams are the family of Muḥammad.” He said, “You are ruined and have ruined others. Did not you and I hear Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: ‘Whoever dies while there is no Imam over him dies a death of Jāhiliyyah’?” So I said, “Yes, by my life.”

And three days before that, or about that, I had gone in to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and Allah granted recognition. So I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), “Indeed Sālim said to me such and such.” He said: So he said, “O Abū ʿUbaydah, no one from among us dies until he leaves behind, after him, one who acts with the like of his deeds, follows his path, and calls to what he called to.”

O Abū ʿUbaydah, what was given to Dāwūd was not withheld from being given to Sulaymān. Then he said, “O Abū ʿUbaydah, when the Qāʾim of the family of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) rises, he will judge with the judgment of Dāwūd and Sulaymān, not asking for evidence.”

key_terms.إِمَامُكَ: your divinely designated Imam whose authority must be recognized
key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَةَ: recognition and true knowledge of the Imam
key_terms.بَيِّنَةً: formal outward proof or evidentiary testimony
key_terms.بِحُكْمِ دَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ: with the mode of judgment of Dāwūd and Sulaymān through divinely granted knowledge
key_terms.سِيرَتِهِ: his way, conduct, and mode of guidance
key_terms.قَائِمُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the rising Imam from the family of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً: a death resembling the state of pre-Islamic ignorance due to lacking recognition of the Imam
key_terms.يُخَلِّفَ: to leave behind a successor after oneself

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith prove continuous Imamate after the death of an Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the confusion after the passing of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) and affirms that the earth is never left without a rightful Imam from Ahl al-Bayt. It also states that each Imam is succeeded by one who continues his mission, and it points to the Qāʾim of آلُ مُحَمَّدٍ (صلى الله عليه وآله) who will judge with divinely granted knowledge like Dāwūd and Sulaymān.
